readme:
# Google Patents Detail Scraper

Get the full record of a patent from its [Google Patents](https://patents.google.com) page. Give the actor patent numbers or patent page links and it returns one row per patent: title, abstract, claims, inventors, assignees, dates, legal status, classifications, family, citations, legal events, PDF and drawings.

Only public patent pages are read, and only the paths the site allows for automated access (`/patent/`). Search pages are not used. If you need to find patent numbers first, use the search on patents.google.com, then paste the numbers here.

## What you get

- Publication number, country, kind code, title and page link
- Abstract and all claims as a list of texts, plus the claim count
- Description: the first characters you ask for (default 5,000) and the full length
- Inventors, original assignees and current assignees
- Application number, priority, filing, publication and grant dates, prior art date
- Legal status and expiry date when the page shows them
- Classification codes (CPC) with descriptions, and the list of most specific codes
- Technology areas, prior art keywords and defined terms
- Family id, family applications, other publications, family members by country
- Citations, patents that cite this one, family citations and similar documents, each with number, link, title, dates and assignee
- Legal events with date, code, title and details, and the event timeline
- PDF link, drawing and thumbnail links, and links to patent office pages
- Optional: also read the patents linked from each page

## Pricing

You pay per event.

| Event name | When it is charged | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `actor-start` | Once per run, together with the first patent delivered | $0.001 |
| `google-patent-result` | For each patent saved to the dataset | $3.00 per 1,000 |

A run that finds no patent is not charged. The actor stops cleanly when your maximum charge per run is reached.

## Input

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `patentNumbers` | list | Numbers such as `US9000000B2`, `EP1000000A1` or `WO2013138362A1`. Spaces, commas and dashes are ignored. |
| `startUrls` | list of links | Links that start with `https://patents.google.com/patent/`. Other links, such as search pages, are refused with a message. |
| `language` | text | Page language code, default `en`. |
| `followCitations` | true or false | Also read patents linked from each page (citations, cited by, similar documents). Default false. |
| `maxResults` | number | Maximum patents in total, including the ones you listed. Default 50. |
| `descriptionChars` | number | Characters of description text to return. Default 5000. Use 0 to return only the length. |

Leave the input empty to run a small demo: patent US9000000B2.

Each patent is one page request, and the actor reads one page at a time with a pause between pages. A run of 40 patents takes about a minute.

### Example: a list of patents

```json
{
  "patentNumbers": ["US9000000B2", "EP1000000A1", "US5000000A"],
  "descriptionChars": 2000
}
```

### Example: start from one patent and follow its links

```json
{
  "patentNumbers": ["US9000000B2"],
  "followCitations": true,
  "maxResults": 40
}
```

Patents are read in order: the ones you listed first, then the ones linked from them (citations, then cited by, then similar documents), until `maxResults` is reached.

### Example: patent page links

```json
{
  "startUrls": ["https://patents.google.com/patent/US9000000B2/en"]
}
```

Fields without a value are returned as `null` or as an empty list. The dataset has more fields than shown here, see the Output tab.

## Limitations

- Only `/patent/` pages are read. Searching by keyword, inventor or date is not possible with this actor.
- The description text is cut at `descriptionChars` to keep rows small. The full length is in `descriptionLength`.
- Citation lists are capped at 500 entries per list. The full count is in `citationsCount` and `citedByCount`.
- The list of defined terms is capped at 100 entries.
- Legal status, expiry and current assignee are shown by Google Patents as an assumption, not a legal conclusion. Check the patent office record before relying on them.
- Some older or foreign patents have no claims, abstract or legal events on the page, and those fields are empty.
- A patent number that has no page returns no row. If none of your numbers has a page, the run ends with a message and nothing is charged.
- The page is sometimes refused. The actor retries once. If every page is refused, the run ends with an error and no charge.

## FAQ

**Which links are accepted?**
Links that start with `https://patents.google.com/patent/`. Search result links and other pages are refused, and the status message says why.

**What does a number without a kind code do?**
A number such as `US9000000` is sent as it is. Google Patents may redirect it to the full number, or may have no page. Use the full number with the kind code when you can.

**Does the same patent appear twice?**
No. Each publication number is returned once per run, even when it is linked from several pages.

**How many patents does `followCitations` read?**
Up to `maxResults` in total. Every patent read is one row and one charge, so set `maxResults` to the number you are willing to pay for.

**Is a run restarted safely?**
Yes. Progress is saved after every patent. If a run is moved to another server it continues where it stopped, without duplicate rows and without charging twice.

**Can I use the data for commercial purposes?**
You are responsible for how you use the data and for following the terms of Google Patents and the rules that apply to you.
